text.p: **BIRTHDAYS**
Italian adventurer GIOVANNI CASANOVA, famous for his amorous 'conquests', was born in 1725.
English actor CHARLES YOUNG, who played Shakespearean roles in Australia, was born in 1819.
American actor SPENCER TRACY, who won Oscars two years running for "Captains Courageous" in 1937 and "Boys Town" in 1938, was born in 1900.
Austrian conductor HERBERT VON KARAJAN was born in 1908.
American actress BETTE DAVIS, best known for her performance in "Whatever Happened To Baby Jane?", was born in 1908.
American actor GREGORY PECK was born in 1916.

Co-founder of the 'Platters' TONY WILLIAMS was born in 1928. He was also the lead singer on all of their major hits. In 1954 he made his first recordings including "Only You". It was rejected by the record company Federal. In 1955 the band signed with the Mercury record company and their hits included "Only You" (1955), "The Great Pretender" (1955), "My Prayer" (1956) and "Smoke Gets In Your Eyes" (1958).

UK singer/songwriter with the 'Hollies' ALLAN CLARKE was born in 1941. An EMI producer, hunting for another 'Beatles', discovered the 'Hollies' in Liverpool's Cavern Club. Their biggest hits were "Just One Look" (1964), "I'm Alive" (1965), "I Can't Let Go' (1966), "Bus Stop" (1966), "Carrie-Anne" (1967), "He Ain't Heavy He's My Brother" (1969), "Long Cool Woman In A Black Dress" (1972) and "The Air That I Breathe" (1974).
AGNETHA from 'Abba' fame was born in 1950. The Swedish singer's full name is AGNETHA ASE FALTSKOG.
US singer PIA ZADORA was born in 1955. She had an international hit with JERMAINE JACKSON with "When The Rain Begins To Fall" (1984).
She also appeared in the films "Butterfly" (1982), "A Lonely Lady" (1983) and "Hairspray" (1988).
**EVENTS**
1895 : A trial began at the Old Bailey in London, in
which playwright OSCAR WILDE sued the MARQUESS OF QUEENSBURY for libel, after she had allegedly accused him of sodomy.
1915 : The first black heavyweight boxing champion JACK
JOHNSON, lost his title to "great white hope" JESS WILLARD.
1923 : The man who discovered the tomb of TUTANKHAMUN,

LORD CARNARVON, died of a mosquito bite. It was claimed he was the first victim of TUTANKHAMUN'S CURSE, because the tiny bite was in the same position as a blemmish on the body of the boy king. Seven years after the death of CARNARVON, only two of the original team responsible for the discovery of the tomb were still alive.
1932 : Legendary horse PHAR LAP died at Menlo Park in
California. It was first thought that PHAR LAP had been deliberately poisoned, but it was later found that he died of colic after eating grass that contained weed killer.
1944 : Germany began the deportation of Jews from
Hungary.
1955 : British Prime Minister WINSTON CHURCHILL announced
his resignation, after suffering a crippling stroke 2 years earlier.
1960 : The movie "BEN HUR" won 10 Oscars.
1964 : Commander of the Pacific Forces during World War
Two, GENERAL DOUGLAS MACARTHUR, died. He was born in Little Rock, Arkansas, and retired from the Army in 1950.
1966 : Champion Australian jockey DARBY MUNRO died. He
rode 3 Melbourne Cup winners, 5 Victoria Derby winners, 4 W.S COX Plates, 5 AJC Derbies, 3 Sydney Cups, 2 Epsoms and 2 Doncaster Handicaps.
1982 : Britain sent out a taskforce to oust Argentinian
troops from the Falkland Islands.
1987 : The Australian Government set aside three million
dollars for an AIDS education campaign.
1989 : Vietnam announced the withdrawal of its troops
from Cambodia, to be completed by September.
1989 : The end of communist rule in Poland came into
view, with the independent trade union federation SOLADARITY winning the right to contest free elections.
1991 : United States President GEORGE BUSH approved the
supply of food-aid to Kurdish refugees in Northern Iraq.
1994 : The Queensland Criminal Justice Commission handed

down its report on the death of young Aboriginal dancer DANIEL YOCK. The commission recommended that no charges be laid against the arresting police officers. YOCK had died in the carpark of the Brisbane watch-house. The report attracted protests by Aboriginal groups.
